description: glibc (glibc-2.39-142.el10_2) built in stage0 vs the 221 official RPMs (packages/glibc.nix, docs/glibc.md). Every rule is a difference that is understood and accepted; anything else fails the check.

allow.reason: glibc.spec builds glibc32 (the i686 libraries packaged for x86_64, used by Rocky's gcc multilib build) but Rocky does not publish it in BaseOS/AppStream/CRB, so the lock has no official RPM
glibc.spec's cross-compiler sysroot package; built by Rocky but not published in any repo of the lock
glibc.spec builds it on x86_64; Rocky does not publish it in any repo of the lock

POSIX_V7_LP64_OFF64 and XBS5_LP64_OFF64 are hard links to one getconf binary (one build-id); rpm names the build-id links <id> and <id>.2 in file-walk (readdir) order, which depends on the build filesystem (overlayfs here, xfs/ext4 on Rocky's builders). Same two targets on both sides

memusagestat links libgd.so.3, which the stage0 glibc buildroot takes from nixpkgs (gd 2.3.3, bootstrap/glibc-build-deps.nix); nixpkgs' libgd defines gdFontLarge/gdFontSmall 32-byte aligned (Rocky's gd-2.3.3-22.el10: 8-byte), and ld places the copy-relocated objects by the defining DSO's alignment: .bss 0x78/align 32 vs 0x50/align 16, so the 3 copy-relocated symbols move (.dynsym values, .rela.dyn offsets, RIP-relative displacements in .text) and .dynstr follows libgd's symbol order. The code is identical (verified with displacement-normalized objdump), dynamic symbols/versions/NEEDED are equal (elf.dynsym etc. are not allowed here). Goes away when the buildroot links Rocky's libgd (stage1; docs/glibc.md, Known differences)
the RW PT_LOAD memsz follows the .bss size (see elf.alloc:/usr/bin/memusagestat:.bss)
